title: Ideas Are Free, Execution Is Everything
about:
A keynote-driven course from The Platform Nigeria, taught by Tosin Eniolorunda, founder and CEO of Moniepoint, the fintech he and his co-founder built from scratch in 2015 into one of Africa's largest payment platforms.

His argument is blunt: an idea is free and a dime a dozen, and the biggest obstacle you will face is yourself. What separates a unicorn from a graveyard of brilliant ideas is execution. To execute, Tosin gives a mental model of seven internal principles that you use to build a great organization, and to diagnose it when something goes wrong: goals, structure, people, incentives, context, systems, and governance.
benefits:
• Treat execution, not ideas, as the thing that actually builds a business
  • Master the inner game: conquer yourself before the market
  • Turn goals into written numbers and know what winning looks like
  • Build a structure that serves the goal, not your most talented individual
  • Hire for the traits that let an organization scale, starting with customer obsession
  • Motivate people with meaning, mastery, membership, and money, in that order
  • Run the machine with incentives, context, systems, and governance, and diagnose drift with all seven principles

steps.title: From software to a unicorn: execution at scale

item.content:
Tosin opens with the journey from a small idea to one of Africa's largest payment platforms, built from scratch and purely Nigerian.

In this lesson

  • Stand on the shoulders of a giant: join where the state of the art already is, then launch
  • Why he traded a hardware dream for software
  • The scale execution actually built: 8 of 10 offline transactions, millions of businesses, billions processed

steps.title: Ideas are free, execution is everything

item.content:
The thesis the whole talk turns on.

In this lesson

  • An idea is a dime a dozen, and it is not waiting for you
  • Execution is the only thing that counts
  • Pick the idea up and truly execute it

Before the market, the entrepreneur has to win the inner game.

In this lesson

  • The biggest battles are internal: conquer yourself and you conquer the world
  • Keep a calm mind against anxiety
  • Build a mental model shaped by reality, conviction, and what works, the seven principles ahead

item.content:
Principle one of seven. A goal that cannot become a number on paper is just vibes.

In this lesson

  • Write the number down: Tosin's founding goal was 100 million dollars
  • The pitch to early hires: own one percent of the vision
  • Know your numbers, revenue, margin, cash flow, profit, and know what winning looks like

Principle two. How Moniepoint reached every corner of Nigeria.

In this lesson

  • Win it the way elections are won: ward to local government to state to national
  • Structure serves the goal, not your most talented individual
  • Make ownership unmistakable, and reduce the dependencies in the way

item.content:
Principle three, and the hardest to satisfy.

In this lesson

  • The right people in the right roles
  • Hundreds of open roles, and a real struggle to fill them well
  • You compete with the world, so hire for the global standard, not the local one

steps.title: Customer obsession: when customers love you, money follows

item.content:
The first and most important trait to hire for.

In this lesson

  • Make customers love you, ahead of even revenue
  • Three levels of love: basic, performative, and delighter
  • Reliability in an unreliable country, instant settlement, and warnings that delight
  • A delighter becomes basic over time, so you never stop improving

steps.title: From craft to candor: the rest of the traits

item.content:
The traits that let an organization scale.

In this lesson

  • Craft, and systems that do not rely on human memory
  • Ownership and urgency
  • No ego, candor, integrity, and a meritocracy that keeps politics out

item.content:
Principle four. The traits are what you expect of people; the four Ms are what they expect of you.

In this lesson

  • Meaning: people need to see how the mission fits their own destiny
  • Mastery: keep them challenged
  • Membership: a tribe to belong to
  • Money, last of all, once basic needs are met it is not the highest

Principles five and six.

In this lesson

  • Incentivize the behaviour: commissions, rewards, public recognition
  • Context: sometimes the person is not bad, it is your own problem
  • Give people the full picture so they can make the right calls

Principle seven, plus the recap that ties the model together.

In this lesson

  • Systems encode judgment, because human memory is not trustworthy
  • Governance corrects the drift between reality and the plan
  • Use all seven principles to diagnose anything that goes wrong
